# Why the Sky Is Blue

The sky appears blue (on clear, sunny days) because of **Rayleigh scattering** — a phenomenon where light, particularly short wavelengths like blue and violet, is scattered more strongly by air molecules than longer wavelengths like red and orange.

## The Key Physics

Sunlight is made up of all colors of the visible spectrum (roughly 400–700 nanometers). Blue/violet light (~400–425 nm) has the **shortest wavelengths**, meaning it travels in shorter, choppier waves that make it **more likely to bounce off** molecules of nitrogen (N₂) and oxygen
